headline: High data-leakage and cascading-error risk: Khoj can read indexed notes while ComfyUI can ingest files, creating unsafe default handoffs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI is offline and has no filesystem read/write or MCP, so direct injection paths are limited. Khoj can read indexed documents and uses RAG/web search, so if ComfyUI outputs are manually copied into Khoj, prompt-like content could be reinterpreted. The pair lacks a documented shared channel, so this is low rather than medium.
conditions: IF ComfyUI outputs are manually pasted into Khoj chat or notes
IF Khoj indexes ComfyUI-generated text artifacts as trusted instructions
mitigations: Avoid copying raw model outputs into Khoj prompts
Prefix imported ComfyUI text as untrusted data
Use separate workspaces for generation and retrieval
Review any prompt templates before indexing
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to retrieved content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Khoj reads indexed personal notes/files and can send content to a cloud or self-hosted server; ComfyUI handles images, videos, audio, and model assets. Even without a shared filesystem, a user can move sensitive outputs from ComfyUI into Khoj for retrieval, exposing those data classes in default workflows. The pair therefore creates a plausible sensitive-data flow.
conditions: IF ComfyUI-generated images, workflows, or seeds are imported into Khoj
IF Khoj is configured with cloud search providers or remote server storage
mitigations: Keep ComfyUI outputs out of Khoj indexes
Disable remote search providers in Khoj
Store sensitive assets in a separate vault
Restrict Khoj to non-sensitive collections
requires-engineering: enforce per-collection access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ComfyUI cannot write files or modify git state, while Khoj also lacks filesystem write and git mutation. Both can read or process content, but they do not overlap on unrestricted mutable resources, so direct write-write conflict is unlikely. The main interaction is read-side only, which keeps this low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable directory through external orchestration
IF an operator grants additional write permissions not present in the profiles
mitigations: Keep both agents on read-only mounts
Separate model asset directories from note indexes
Avoid shared git worktrees
Audit any external orchestrator permissions
requires-engineering: add locking for shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Khoj can treat retrieved content as authoritative in a conversational RAG flow, while ComfyUI can generate workflows, prompts, and assets that may be reused downstream. If ComfyUI output is fed into Khoj without verification, errors or hallucinated metadata can cascade into later answers or actions. The pair lacks a built-in verification bridge, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF ComfyUI-generated prompts, captions, or workflow metadata are imported into Khoj
IF Khoj answers are used as authoritative summaries without human review
mitigations: Mark ComfyUI outputs as unverified in Khoj
Require human review before reusing generated metadata
Separate generation and retrieval tasks
Use citation prompts in Khoj
requires-engineering: add validation against source artifacts

E_compliance.rationale: Khoj explicitly touches personal notes and indexed documents and may use cloud or self-hosted servers, while ComfyUI handles media and model assets offline. If personal or regulated content from ComfyUI workflows is indexed into Khoj, retention and residency policies can diverge. The profiles do not show a shared compliance control, so the mismatch is a medium compliance risk.
conditions: IF regulated content from ComfyUI is indexed into Khoj
IF Khoj is deployed with retention or residency settings different from the source workflow
mitigations: Exclude regulated assets from Khoj indexing
Document retention settings for both systems
Use self-hosted Khoj for sensitive collections
Review data residency before import
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion policies
